Single y- come paradigm, compared with2013yuun and Palula y-. Perfective yaal, imperfective yuun, future/other endings require separate morphology; linking root family does not assert every form directly continues yāti or decide competing ā-gata ancestry of the perfective.

gìin matches Palula ghin- take and the voiced-aspiration/Low comparison inTable10. The perfective formation needs its own lineage; do not infer ancestry from generic take gloss or its Low alone.
Reduced ä indefinite article corresponds to2013äk one and regional ēka grammaticalization. Accent loss in a clitic/article is not a counterexample to lexical numeral accent.
fäsälá agreement is the regional Arabic-origin faisala decision word; final High belongs to a contact noun and is not evidence for Sanskrit accent inheritance.
suwaa same lexeme as2013all; sourcegraph13726stoma praise is unsupported. A possible mass/totality base requires independent segmental history; no replacement accepted.
tée corresponds exactly to2013tee linked tathāpi; tadā is a competing particle history. Preserve provisional attribution and do not use the conjunction for strict inherited noun accent.

Identical2013nikhät came out underupaskad/skad-family prefixed niḥ form; appear is a semantic extension of emerge. Compare imperfnikhuun separately; input formation may be a modern suppletive paradigm.
bäkhin is a suffixed arm noun, plausibly related to regional bāhu/bāhaka formations, but kh and ending need an independently supported derivation. Unmarked tone cannot settle it.
kiteek quantifier contains interrogative amount material pluspossibleek one. Whole form should not be assigned to a generic much adjective; exact internal boundary and older input unresolved.

täpoos is the regional tapos inquiry/ask word also recorded Palula; likely contact-derived but exact donor chain not established here. Compound light-verb syntax matters; no inherited accent inference.
Personal name Aslam; no Old Indo-Aryan etymon expected in this accent test.
=dii is a postpositional clitic; possible locative/deictic source needs grammatical reconstruction. Equals sign explicitly excludes independent word-accent treatment.

khaál belongs eat khā paradigm. Perfective l cannot be equated directly with old khādita without evaluating analogical -il/-al morphology; final High is real but its historical cell needs separate treatment.
patä adverb in come back is source-gloss uncertain. Compare pṛṣṭha back and prati returnward particles; neither semantic resemblance establishes identity. No accepted link.
phäṇoos ball has possible inflated/rounded formation but no demonstrated cognate in the compared families. Retain unknown tone and ancestry.
čädeer basket does not follow from generic bag sthavi; possible suffix eer requires a supported root, not shape-only matching.
ic̣ matches regional ṛkṣa bear reflexes with vocalic-r front vowel and reduced kṣ; exact same inherited animal noun. Unmarked tone remains unknown.

bìl became is the b- perfective related to bhūta andregionalbulo/bhilu. Final l may include modern perfective morphology; Low agrees with historical voiced aspiration, but direct segment-by-segment -ta outcome is not assumed.

buṣil- hunger predicate plausibly shares bubhukṣaka hungry family with Palula/Sawi buċhal/buċhaal; forms add inchoative andtense material. Segmental intermediate andsuffixes need reconstruction; not a direct old adjective accent test.
ḍä̀är identical2013form, related regional *ḍhiḍḍha belly; Low corresponds to lost voiced aspiration. The expressive base is not Vedic-accented evidence.
sängaás bench is segmentally distinct from generic seat roots; possible compound but neither member independently established. Retain final High as lexical observation.
seekäl bicycle andbas bus are recognizable recent transport loans; no inherited Old Indo-Aryan accent comparison.
gän corresponds regional ghaná compact/big andPalula gháanu; loss of aspiration andapocope require separate analysis. Unmarked tone is not explicit zero.
Examples big head and a big house contain multiple lexical words. Big element shares ghaná family, but no whole-phrase etymon or one accent outcome is assigned.
päṣin closelycontinues pakṣin bird with preserved in-suffix andregional kṣ>s/c̣. This is an independently suffixed formation distinct from sparrow čikar.

čikaar/čikär bird may be regional expressive or hunting/bird name; a caṭaka match does not explain k/r andquantity securely. Two forms may involve inflection/recording differences; High confirmed only where marked.

ingär/ingäraan are a noun andexpanded inflection, plausibly related to aṅgāra coal through occupational derivation; do not equate with unrelated ḍomba solely by occupation. Derivation andcontact history remain open.
taa blanket/cloak is too short to identify from the generic gloss; no supported kambala correspondence. Source enclitic waa belongs outside noun.
raat corresponds Palula rat andregional rakta blood with kt simplification andsecondary length. HultmanTable9 explicitly zero tone, a critical apocope/cluster control.
kitaáb Arabic-origin regional book loan; kitaábuni adds native plural/case material while preserving root High. Useful contact morphology, not Vedic inheritance.
sunduu box plausibly regional ṣandūq loan with final-stop loss; sourceglossuncertain. No inherited accent link asserted.
púu boy is the2013/Palula phoó family pṓta; HultmanTable9 explicitly earlyHigh. Derivational stages ā/ō and aspiration differ from ordinary inherited long-root nouns.
läḍkur boy resembles regional laṛkā with expanded kur/kuj plural alternation; borrowing versus inherited expressive formation unresolved. Multiple forms encode number/case, not independent etyma.
puṭooš child likely derived from putra/putta family with additional ooš material. Its suffix cannot be omitted in an accent comparison; no simple pūta/pota identification accepted.

geél bread/food corresponds Palula gúuli round loaf family gōla; fronting andloss of final vowel plausible but derivational vowel grade uncertain. Retain as provisional, not strict inherited-accent control.
dra same2013Kalkbrother, regional bhrātr̥ reflex with initial cluster transformation. No printed tone here; kinship paradigm important.
ǰäleen resembles regional jal- burn family, but linking to dahyate from English alone would hide different segmental histories. Modern -een is inflectional.
mäni called is a quoted naming construction; compare regional man-/bhan- say only afterchecking sourceparadigm. No simple noun ancestor asserted.

buun ability construction shares Kalkb- be/become morphology, not direct causative bhāvayati merely because Palula ability bhuu was indexed there. Unmarked tone is uncertain, possible grammatical reduction.
ṣaa causee marker is grammatical relation marking; its lexical origin must be established separately. No segmentally justified old noun link.
šää bed/charpoy likely regional śayyā family but precise formation andvowel history not verified; not assigned simply togeneric bedgloss.
čhinil belongs cut/split chind/chin root; modern perfective -il must be separated from old chinna. No direct participial accent mapping without source paradigm.
šukooḍ/šugooḍ is one cloak lexeme with voicingvariation; could be regional garment loan/compound. No proposed Sanskrit link has adequate segmental support.
šidäl exact2013reflex of śītala cold. Final l reflects adjectival formation, modern tone unmarked; not a c̣aa fear/chill root substitute.
